newsitem.title: USA: CWB not aware of problems with India-bound wheat.
newsitem.headline: CWB not aware of problems with India-bound wheat.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board is not aware of any problems with Canadian wheat destined for India and there has been no contact between the two countries regarding Canadian wheat not meeting contract specifications, a CWB spokesman told Reuters.
"The important part is what we have agreed to sell, we will be selling," said Jim Pietryk, the CWB spokesman.
An Indian newspaper report that Canadian wheat failed phytosanitary tests contributed to wheat price gains at U.S. commodity exchanges Tuesday.

India's State Trading Corporation (STC) also denied the allegations, which were made in India's Statesman newspaper. An STC official in New Delhi told Reuters that Canadian wheat has met wheat import standards set in 1992.
The Statesman newspaper said wheat samples from Canada failed the phytosanitary tests. The CWB would not comment on if Canadian wheat had been tested in India.
An STC official said India had contracted for 250,000 tonnes of imports from the Canadian Wheat Board and the first shipments were due in February.
CWB's Pietryk said some Indian vessels were arriving at the Vancouver port but none have been loaded.
"There is a bit of a lineup on the West Coast because of the weather," he said. "No wheat (bound for India) has been loaded yet."

Additionally, India was scheduled to tender late Tuesday for 50,000 tonnes or more of optional-origin wheat for March arrival. U.S. exporters said India would likely buy Australian or U.S. hard wheat.
